claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially in a high-temperature BCC state.
Local compositional fluctuations arise during cooling from the high-temperature BCC state.
Cooling-induced compositional fluctuations promote the formation of nanoscale B2-type or similar ordered clusters.
The ordered clusters form through a martensitic-like, diffusionless or low-diffusivity ordering event.
B2-type ordered clusters heterogeneously nucleate during cooling.
The cooling-induced ordered domains serve as nucleation sites for further phase evolution during subsequent thermal exposure.
Cooling rate modulates the density and distribution of the ordered clusters.
Differences in ordered-cluster density and distribution determine the ultimate phase assemblage after thermal exposure.
Slow cooling permits local compositional segregation and transient ordering.
Slow-cooled samples will contain a higher density and more uniform distribution of B2-ordered clusters than rapidly cooled samples.
Slow-cooled samples will form secondary phases during a subsequent isothermal hold.
Rapid cooling suppresses local ordering and leaves fewer ordered precursors.
Rapidly cooled samples will retain a more metastable, largely untransformed BCC matrix.
Rapidly cooled samples will have a reduced propensity for phase decomposition during subsequent thermal exposure.
An intermediate thermal-exposure regime permits metastable ordered clusters to grow or transform.
A sufficiently high thermal-exposure temperature re-homogenizes the microstructure and suppresses the proposed mechanism.
Residual stresses and microsegregation may also influence the phase evolution.
The controlled comparison uses rapidly and slowly cooled samples from the same batch, followed by an identical isothermal hold below the BCC stability limit.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis characterizes ordering as diffusion-free or diffusionless, while the applicability conditions require slow cooling to permit compositional segregation. Compositional segregation normally requires diffusion, so the proposed event alternates ambiguously between a diffusionless transformation and a diffusion-controlled process.
